Tracki GPS Tracker for Vehicles, Car, Kids, Dogs, Motorcycle. 4G LTE GPS Tracking Device. Unlimited Distance US & Worldwide. Small Portable Real time Mini Magnetic. Subscription Needed Hi. This review is long overdue. I bought these because I was having a problem with a neighbor trespassing on my Mountain property. We had put up numerous game cameras to catch him in the act sadly this unscrupulous character stole those game cameras.

Frustrated as we felt the local sheriff wouldn’t do anything unless we actually caught him red-handed, I bought cheap game cameras and gutted them. I bought four of these devices and installed them behind the battery cover for these now gutted game cameras.

We make sure to put 2 of them up when he was outside and watching. Seven hours later I was sitting on the sofa and evening and I got an alert that one of the trackers started moving. I couldn’t believe this was correct and grabbed my wife while I kept refreshing the tracker all the while taking screen grabs from my phone. We called the sheriff department and they came out and were amazed at the specificity of where the tracker had been.

While I was talking to the deputies in my driveway we heard the neighbor start up his ATV and I made a comment that he’s up to no good.

When we looked at the final data at the moment The neighbor started his ATV one of the trackers all of a sudden went from zero and 1 mph to 6 mph. And then one the trackers stopped moving and was showing back on my property. Another tracker was still showing on the neighbors property and the deputies were able to go right to the spot I showed them on the map in the app and get it.

Clearly, he realized something was up with all the sheriff deputies driving by and tried to get rid of the evidence.

The deputies asked me to send them the times and locations for their report and I said I’ll do you better and exported it all to an excel spreadsheet that had hyperlinks to where the tracker was at anytime. It also included the GPS lat/long. You can totally customize the report you want to see down to the exact hour!

My neighbor was cited for trespassing, theft and criminal mischief.

I also called the company and spoke with Stephen as the one tracker that got thrown back into my property had a cracked battery door. They freely mailed me out a replacement cover. Great product backed up with fantastic customer service.

I pay the month to month plan of $20/tracker and am totally satisfied. Don’t even complain about the monthly, because if something is valuable enough for you to need to track it, then $20 bucks a month is nothing.

And BTW, this thing is tiny!
text_fidelity_b: Tracki GPS Tracker for Vehicles, Car, Kids, Dogs, Motorcycle. 4G LTE GPS Tracking Device. Unlimited Distance US & Worldwide. Small Portable Real time Mini Magnetic. Subscription Needed

text_fidelity_a:
FYHXele Computer Monitor, Gaming Monitor 24 Inch 75Hz, IPS FHD 1080P, 2xHDMI, USB Type-C, Built-in Speakers, Adaptive Sync, VESA for Office Home, Black I’ve been using the FYHXele 24 Inch Monitor (75Hz version) for the last month, and it has totally spoiled me for playing games on my Switch! The monitor has built-in speakers, so I can hear a game’s music while playing. It’s a small but nice feature; I can easily switch the input from my laptop to my Switch and not have to rearrange my whole desk to play games.

The picture is bright and vibrant. I’ve been playing Hades for the last month and it looks SO good on this screen. Bright and crisp, even if I play during the day. I also use the monitor as a second display for work, it’s good for that too, either as a streaming display or for text and spreadsheets.

I use it with my MacBook Pro, the monitor has 2 HDMI inputs and 1 USB-C. The USB-C port doesn’t support passthrough charging.

A VESA plate is included, which was a nice plus. I do use a monitor arm because I don’t like the stand this monitor comes with. The angle and height are not adjustable at all, and I didn’t like the default angle. The base is 9 inches by 7 inches, so it has a large footprint. I also don’t love the “FYHXele” printed in white at the bottom of the screen.

The power cable is relatively short, only 50 inches. It’s an AC adapter, not a power brick. The box also includes an HDMI cable -- another nice plus -- but unfortunately my cable had a cut in the coating, so I could see the copper wire.

Overall, I think this is a decent budget monitor. I never want to play my Switch in handheld mode anymore, the picture quality has spoiled me that much. The dual HDMI inputs make it easy to switch between work and fun; I’ve also used this as a Discord display, rotated 90° on a VESA arm.
text_fidelity_b: FYHXele Computer Monitor, Gaming Monitor 24 Inch 75Hz, IPS FHD 1080P, 2xHDMI, USB Type-C, Built-in Speakers, Adaptive Sync, VESA for Office Home, Black

text_fidelity_a:
Sony WHXB900N Noise Cancelling Headphones, Wireless Bluetooth Over the Ear Headset - Blue (Amazon Exclusive) Sony WH-XB900N Wireless Noise Canceling Extra Bass Headphones have great sound quality. Plus, for an over the ear headphone they are surprisingly lightweight. I also like how they bend to fold up and are really pliable. However, that's really where the greatness stops. Pairing these with any device I own is difficult or doesn't happen at all. These will not pair with my laptop. My laptop sees it's there. It claims it's playing from the headphones, but alas it does not most of the time. In addition, these will not play from iTunes. So, if you have an Apple device forget it. These will not pair with my iPhone 5. For two reasons, first, these are terrible with Apple devices/software and second, you must have the App to pair the headphones, which if you have an older phone won't happen because the App is only compatible with certain iOS systems. As much as I am angry with Apple for stopping all updates for older Apple devices (which work just fine otherwise), it's equally frustrating with App developers who do not design their Apps to be compatible with the older systems. So, most of my experience with these headphones is through the AUX jack.

Therefore, the sound quality is really good. I listen to a lot of hiphop and the bass is spot on. However, I do listen other types of music (pretty much everything) and I would have to say listening to Beethoven's 6th and Old Blind Dogs was a nice experience as well! The noise cancelling is a joke. I can hear everything around me still. In fact, I'm currently wearing these as I type this review and can hear the click clack of the keys, my son bump around upstairs, and my father just call my name. So, if you wear these on public transportation or at work, you're gonna hear everything as usual. But they are good headphones and comfortable on my ears.

The instructions are ridiculous. Can we stop with the picture instructions? They make no sense. I need words and should not have to depend on internet video reviews to get clarity on how to use anything. There is a way to play, pause, volume down/up by tapping or swiping, but I have no idea how to do it. Sometimes it works, sometimes not. They have a long battery life. I charged these weeks ago and they still have a charge as I use them now.

So, these have a great sound quality, the noise cancellation doesn't do anything, and you need to pair these with non-Apple devices.
text_fidelity_b: Sony WHXB900N Noise Cancelling Headphones, Wireless Bluetooth Over the Ear Headset - Blue (Amazon Exclusive)

text_fidelity_a:
Nikon D5000 12.3 MP DX Digital SLR Camera with 18-55mm f/3.5-5.6G VR Lens and 2.7-inch Vari-angle LCD My D5000 was delivered yesterday evening while I was at work. The lovely wife opened the box enough to pull the battery out and charge it for me. After a grueling 12 hour shift at work I had forgotten about my new toy.

I had purchased the D5000 w/ 18/55 kit lens then separately purchased a 55/200 VR kit lens. It was cheaper that way. Go figure.

After many doggie slobbers when I arrived home I noticed the D5000 box on the kitchen table. My heart started palpating. I tried to control my self to no avail. My new toy was here! I carefully unpacked everything. I actually followed the quick start guide and was ready in no time.

I'm a big guy with the requisite big hands. The D5000 felt good in my hands. Not too heavy, not too light. The black body was finished with a slightly rough tactile coating. Very nice. My right thumb fit nicely in the thumb spot while my right index finger felt at home on the shutter. With a firm grip on the D5000 I was able to fully articulate my wrist and point the camera in a variety of positions. The camera felt good in my hand. I could tell that I could lug this beauty around for a full day and not get the dreaded "photog's wrist syndrome."

I attached the 18/55 kit lens. The lens seemed to provide a better balance when attached to the body. The VR switch, on the lens, was factory set to OFF. My first few images didn't utilize the VR. I was so excited and getting more excited by the minute that I forgot the properly look at the lens. I could notice the difference between the VR switching. This 18/55 kit lens is quite amazing. Sure it's made out of plastic, but it does a great job. If you don't already have Nikon lenses then the 18/55 kit lens is a no brainer. Well worth it.
As the quick guide said...Frame your first subject...then BAM!

I was looking for subjects to shoot. Since I work nights everyone, except the dog, was asleep. So I can't run around flipping light switches, move knick-knacks, or anything that could involve waking the baby. God forbid I wake the baby. My wife would have my testicles drawn and quartered within 7.9 seconds. Of course it's been raining for 2 days straight. So I'm stuck in the house...with a new camera. No worries!

I really like the D5000. Coming from the "superzoom point & shoot world" this is a welcome, although a little scary, change. I used film SLR cameras up until the late 90's so I have some experience with SLR photography. But the digital advances sure make everything so much easier. I'm not a "all manual all the time" kind of guy. Like most of us, I want the added feature of full-manual to play with, but like having an excellent and fast AUTO feature. I like to spend time with my family when we're all out and about and don't like to fiddle with any settings. The family gives me plenty of time, on my own, to experiment.

I added some images above.
text_fidelity_b: Nikon D5000 12.3 MP DX Digital SLR Camera with 18-55mm f/3.5-5.6G VR Lens and 2.7-inch Vari-angle LCD

These are a four-pack of 64GB thumb drives that come in four colors. The first color, black, that I plugged into the PC hopelessly causes the PC to stall and become unresponsive to the point where I have to pull the power cord out to get the machine to turn off.

text_fidelity_a:
Aokeo USB Microphone, Condenser Podcast Microphone for Computer. Suitable for Recording, Gaming, Desktop, Windows, Mac, YouTube, Streaming, Discord For the price this is a very nice USB microphone, I would agree with other reviewers that it performs on par with or better than similar competing USB condenser mics in this price range such as Blue Snowball or the Behringer C1.

I do wish it came with more accessories though similar to the non-USB version. The Aokeo AK-60 XLR version comes with a scissor boom arm, shock mount and pop filter for the same price.. so if you do happen to have a compatible audio interface with phantom power then I would recommend the XLR version.

The main annoyance with this mic is that when using it in windows 10 the driver does not have native mic gain control option. In many recording programs you can boost the mic gain via other means but if using this mic for gaming or other purposes through the native drivers then you will have to be very close to the mic to produce adequate volume (ie you pretty much need a boom arm) or otherwise you will need to boost gain via external passthrough program such as APO equalizer. I have also tried this mic in linux and the drivers there do have native gain control.

Overall I do think the sound quality and construction of the mic is good for the price and I would recommend it .. just note that if using windows 10 you will probably either need a boom arm or need to use external software to boost the mic gain. A boom arm is strongly recommended anyways to prevent extraneous noises like keyboard clacking, etc..
text_fidelity_b: Aokeo USB Microphone, Condenser Podcast Microphone for Computer. Suitable for Recording, Gaming, Desktop, Windows, Mac, YouTube, Streaming, Discord

Ring Video Doorbell 2 with HD Video, Motion Activated Alerts, Easy Installation Another reviewer mentioned these issues, but I was impulsive and bought it anyways. They are all true.
- I spend a good deal of time adjusting the sensibility settings and using the brackets (both V and H) to reduce false positives, but they are still too many. My door is about 25-30' from the road and if a truck passes, even small cars, "motion detected". You stop giving importance for the sensor.
- I try to answer motion but it takes so long to load (I have an S8, with good wifi) and I got a connection problem way too often. If wasn't another false positive (as usually is), I would have missed the person lurking.
- The recording starts too late. when you go see the recorded video (because you were not able to answer the false positive motion), the video starts way too long after the movement started.
- regarding payments: I have a Piper camera that records up to 1,000 24s videos for free, overwriting after that. It works great. It always worked. Why Ring enforce additional payment is mind-blowing considering what is available on the market.
- I have installed with battery, that was really good because it was easy to install, but on the current pace (75% after 25 days) there is no way it will last the suggested 6 months on the website.

UPDATE: had to completely disable the motion sensor, the false positives were driving me crazy. Not paying the monthly fee. It's too many clicks to get to the screen when somebody actually pushes the button.
Avoid this product and wait for competitors to come up with something better.
UPDATE 2: Now this piece of crap will not enter live view.

MOS Magnetic Cable Organizer- Black I’ve got a few devices now, as probably every body reading this. A smartphone, a tablet, and a cordless mouse that plugs in to charge every week or two. And a couple U.S.B. cords hanging around is a mess. First to find one when needed. Then where to stash it after the use. This little gizmo is the best.
When I first saw it, I’m thinking. Why didn’t I do something like this. And even now, since I have already seen the idea. I could make something like this out of stuff I have around this room. But it’s not expensive. So I want to try and see if they did ‘good’ work. Well, they did.
I really wondered how, a magnetic mount like this could be safe around computers. I thought that the magnetic force might be so pathetically small, as to render such a device useless. But, the little triangle thing, that is the home base for your cable collection; is also magnetized. So a small magnet on the cord, along with the magnetic flux of the mounting surface, makes for a ‘good’ grip. For cables, such as designed for, is perfect. I wanted to put a set of headphones up on this rack. But it never happened. Sure, they would stick, and hold. But then, when other cables would be attached, and detached, the headphones would fall. But cords, are a rock solid stick.
And it is pretty. I’m no designer, but I think it makes my desk look like I care. And it’s a conversation piece. I really like this piece. But I still think, I should have thought of this.

text_fidelity_a:
Belkin VideoLink 3 Powerline Internet Adapter This seemed to be the perfect solution to a problem I was having with obtaining Internet access in my basement. The router is located on the upper floor of the house and, while access is fine in every room above ground, access in the basement has been minimal at best.

Installation was very straightforward - just plug one adapter into the router, the other into the wall socket, and plug in whatever device needs access into one of the three plugs located on the wall socket device.

Overall it works pretty well, but is highly sensitive to noise or heavy draws on the power line. For example, I have a dehumidifier in the basement. When that kicks on, I lose the connection. Sometimes it is regained all by itself, but most of the time I have to either reboot (or power cycle) the device that is plugged in, or unplug and then re-plug the adapter. I tried moving the dehumidifier to a different circuit than the one used by the powerline adapter, and also tried plugging the dehumidifier into a surge protector - no difference. So, I make sure the dehumidifier is off before I use any Internet device.

I've had the same issue with other appliances such as certain vacuums - turn them on, and the connection is lost. There have been no problems with appliances operating in other areas of the house, such as the microwave, laser printers, etc. Just happens when you use the appliance in the same room as the powerline adapter.

But, other than these powerline induced interruptions, the device works well. Speedy connection - can't tell any difference between this and any other WiFi connected device. Well worth taking a look at if you have some WiFi dead zones in your house. Just keep an eye out for someone who is about to use a vacuum when you're at a critical spot in the movie you're streaming!
text_fidelity_b: Belkin VideoLink 3 Powerline Internet Adapter

text_fidelity_a:
Altec Lansing VS2620 Speakers for Computers and MP3 Players (Black) I was initially surprised when I unpacked these speakers because they were a lot larger than I'd expected. In fact, I think they're rather large for laptop speakers unless your laptop doesn't travel the way mine does, around the house or outside of it. You're not going to be carting these speakers along with you. They'll probably end up as speakers for my desktop.

Portability issues aside, they do provide good sound for their size and price point. Tone is crisp and clear, and while you can't do much more than play with the volume and brighten or darken the sound, you can still do some reasonable fine-tuning here. I'm sure there are audiophiles out there who will disagree with me, but then I don't really think that listening to music or watching DVDs on your computer provides optimal enjoyment no matter how good your speakers. It's a convenience, not worth selling your firstborn for.

Apart from the size, my only other quibble is that here is yet another piece of equipment that I have to find a plug for, and a plug that will accommodate yet another bulky transformer. I realize that external speakers which operate on juice from the computer are probably pretty sad little things, and that it's a trade-off, but I really am getting tired of all those black blocks.

But the bottom line is this: I'm sitting here listening to Pandora Radio and it sounds good to me for a change. The sort of good that would get me back to listening on a regular basis. And that, my friends, is the real test of these speakers and their relationship to my laptop. They may not end up attached to the desktop after all.
text_fidelity_b: Altec Lansing VS2620 Speakers for Computers and MP3 Players (Black)

text_fidelity_a:
Kindle Keyboard 3G, Free 3G + Wi-Fi, 6" E Ink Display - includes Special Offers & Sponsored Screensavers This is by far the best ereader on the market.

The bad.

It doesn't do epub and it doesn't connect to the library. This seems like a deal breaker until you try to borrow a book from the library. I have one on hold now (to read on either the nook or the Sony) that should be available in 39 weeks. I'll probably give up and just buy it anyway.

The good.

The speed. The page turns are as fast as the average person can turn a print page. You won't see that "opening book" message the nook displays. When you tell it to open a book, it opens in less than a second. I keep hitting the page turn key just to marvel at how fast it is. I've never seen an ereader this fast. This is perfect.

Store access. Let me run you through buying a book for the various devices. For the Kindle, if you're on the Amazon site you select your book, click buy now, pick up the device and start reading. For the nook, you buy the book, then you turn on the touch screen that keeps turning itself off, you go into the home screen, go to "My Library", select "Update B&N Content" and wait a few minutes. There is no mechanism to automatically push content to the device. For the Sony (I'm using the Daily Edition, which has 3G), you use the custom software (no way to buy from a website), buy the book, then either transfer it via USB, or go to the device, to the store, log into your account (you need to provide your login information each time you go to the store) find the book you bought and click download, then wait. For buying from the device, Kindle is easy and fast, nook is decent, and Sony is unreasonably slow.

The screen. There is no glare, even with the book light on. It's the crispest and easiest to read screen out there. It's beautiful.

Audible integration. Download your books via WiFi or transfer via USB and listen with your device, either through headphones or the speakers. How cool is that? Now if only there were a card reader to store those larger files.

Collections. I have the Kindle 1, so I was first introduced to collections via Sony. It's great to be able to organize so much content. Here you can organize ebooks and audiobooks into collections together. That's one thing Kindle and Sony both have over nook--they treat content the same. Nook is the only one that doesn't let you annotate or bookmark newspapers and magazines, and who wouldn't want to mark an article to refer back to later?

Ease of use. I handed my Kindle 1 to a woman who was too scared of technology to turn on her own laptop. Her husband had to do it for her. I wanted to show her a passage in the Declaration of Independence, and I had the passage on the screen. I didn't instruct her. Moments later, she turned the page and just kept reading, all the way the end. Then she looked at what else I had on the device. An ereader should be as easy and intuitive to use as a print book, and most of us figured those out when we were about 10 months old. Kindle fits that bill.

Social networking. Post passages and comments on them to Twitter and Facebook. You can see what passages other readers have highlighted. This is particularly great for online book clubs.

More language sets. I'm kind of hoping Amazon will sell Japanese language books in the US Kindle store, or let us buy from Amazon.co.jp.

I could go on and on, but what it comes down to is, when it comes down to the core features of an ereader--buying, reading, annotating, and searching a book, Kindle beats the competition hands down. When it comes to extra bells and whistles--organization, commenting to others, web access, text to speech, Kindle beats the competition hands down.

There is no other viable choice any more. Kindle is just too much better than every other device out there.
text_fidelity_b: Kindle Keyboard 3G, Free 3G + Wi-Fi, 6" E Ink Display - includes Special Offers & Sponsored Screensavers

text_fidelity_a:
Sony ICFS79W AM/FM/Weather Band Digital Tuner Shower Radio (White) FM reception is flat out horrible where I live. It's like a radeo dead zone. My home theater system can pull in nothing. My stereo gets a lot of static. I listen almost exclusively online but I'd heard good things about this radio so I decided to give it a try. The reception was amazing. Perfectly clear. No static on FM at all. It sounds beautiful. The weather feed was full of static, but servicable--I ususally can't pull in the weather band at all. AM is average--neither the worse I've heard nor the best. But then, I don't expect much from AM.

It does the FM1, FM2 trick that some cars do. There is no difference. It just lets them repurpose the buttons. I find it odd, but not bad.

The only think I would have changed is how it hangs. If you don't have a shower hook (I don't) it hangs over the shower head. That tilts the entire unit forward. It should either suspend from the shower curtain rack (the strap is oriented the wrong way to do that--it would try to hand perpendicular to the curtain) or reach a better balance point. That's an issue of aesthetics, not function. I'd be worried about sitting it on the edge of the tub, as it is too likely to fall.

The one trick to remember, when sticking the antenna to the shower wall, is that suction cups don't work as well on a wet surface. Thoroughly dry the wall first, then place it. It helps will the issue of the antenna falling.
text_fidelity_b: Sony ICFS79W AM/FM/Weather Band Digital Tuner Shower Radio (White)

text_fidelity_a:
Belkin Verve Folio Case with Stand for Samsung Galaxy Tab 10.1inch (Black) My favorite types of cases are the rigid style that grab onto the edges of the device and do not increase the width or length of the device significantly. This is sort of a hybrid between that style and Belkin's ultrathin folio style.

That's because this one has a "pocket" for the device just like the soft ultrathins, which means you see the screen through a well placed cutout. It also has holes cut for the buttons, lenses, and ports. It is smaller from a length and width perspective than the ultrathin, but a bit deeper because the cover is thicker. It also has cleaner lines, although not as clean as some hard cases.

It also has an elastic strap attached to the cover that can be turned around to hold the case shut. Only time will tell if that stays nice and tight or ends up sagging after use. Really, it doesn't need to be used often as the case will mostly stay shut by itself.

The one thing I don't like is the way you fold the front cover behind the back: it sort of seems too stiff, as if you're not really supposed to. It also folds at both joints, which keeps it from lying completely flat. The ultrathin folio has it beat in that case, although I like the Verve in better in most other ways.

A nice case for your tablet.
text_fidelity_b: Belkin Verve Folio Case with Stand for Samsung Galaxy Tab 10.1inch (Black)
